to 99% (0.99), due to unequal amplification of the original alleles during PCR. Furthermore, the scVAF of wild-type cells is commonly not equal to 0 due to noise generated during PCR amplification and next-generation sequencing. These sources of noise need to be accounted for when calling genotypes. To define the appropriate scVAF thresholds for mutation calling, we use data from WT control cells where the genotype is known a priori to determine the error rate at each locus. We have benchmarked this strategy for defining genotyping thresholds across 16 loci (Figures 23B and 23C). We have found that the probability of WT cells having a scVAF measurement above the threshold used to call cells heterozygous mutant (i.e. false positive mutant calls) was consistently below 0.006.Note: Cells that appear WT for a mutation can either be genuinely WT or there may have been allelic dropout (ADO) of the allele harboring the mutation (Figure 24A), and it is not normally possible to distinguish these two scenarios. However, when a heterozygous germline single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) is present within the genotyping amplicon, this may be used to determine whether both alleles have been sampled in each cell (Figure 24B). Variant calling at the SNP locus is performed in the same way as for the mutations (Figure 24C). By phasing the SNP alleles with the mutation (Figure 24B), it is possible to identify cells in which the mutant allele has dropped out and thus exclude these from the analysis due to the uncertainty regarding their genotype. This also makes it possible to calculate the ADO rate.Figure 24Allelic drop-out controls using germline heterozygous SNPs(A) Schematics of allelic drop-out.(B) Schematic overview of how germline heterozygous SNPs may be phased with mutations in the same genotyping amplicon. Top, when the SNP Alternate (Alt) allele is in-phase with the mutation (i.e. they are located on the same allele), the single-cell variant allele frequency (scVAF) of the mutation and the SNP are correlated. Cells where there was ADO of the mutant allele will have a scVAF close to 0% for both the mutation and the SNP. Bottom, when the SNP Alt allele is out-of-phase with the mutation (i.e. they are located on opposite alleles), the scVAF of the mutation and the SNP are anti-correlated. Cells where there was ADO of the mutant allele will have a scVAF of ∼0% for the mutation but a scVAF of ∼100% for the SNP Alt allele. Plot adapted from our original paper.1(C) Plot of the scVAF distribution for the TET2 rs55838312 germline SNP, comparing cells from a heterozygous sample (NOC117, left of the graph) versus the WT control sample (right of the graph). steps.title: Pilot: Determine optimal PCR cycles
steps.instruction: Perform a pilot experiment to find the PCR cycle number that yields 0.25–0.5 ng/µL cDNA per cell (max 2 ng/µL) after bead purification.

substeps.instruction: Prepare generic lysis buffer (per well: 3.9 µL nuclease‑free water, 6.7 µL 40 % PEG 8000, 0.1 µL 10 % Triton X‑100, 0.33 µL RNase inhibitor (0.5 U/µL), 0.42 µL 10 mM dNTPs each, 0.27 µL protease (1.09 AU/mL), 0.67 µL Oligo(dT)-ISPCR (0.67 µM); total 6 µL per well, dispense into alternate columns of a 96‑well plate).
Store plates at –80 °C (up to 1 month).
FACS‑sort single cells into the lysis plates (leave 2 wells per plate as NTCs), seal with aluminum film and snap‑freeze on dry ice; plates can be stored at –80 °C up to 3 months.
Run RT‑PCR pre‑amplification (omit target‑specific primers) using at least three cycle numbers (e.g., 19, 21, 23 for HSPCs). Double reaction volumes compared to 384‑well protocol.

Dilute amplified cDNA 1:2 with nuclease‑free water, then purify 20 µL of the diluted cDNA with AMPure XP beads (0.6 × beads): equilibrate beads 30 min at 21 °C, add 12 µL beads to a V‑bottom plate, mix with 20 µL diluted cDNA, incubate ≥5 min at 21 °C, magnet 2 min, wash twice with 100 µL 80 % ethanol, air‑dry 2–4 min, elute in 10 µL EB, magnet 2–3 min, transfer supernatant to new plate. Store purified cDNA at –20 °C (≥1 year).
QC cDNA: capillary electrophoresis (Bioanalyzer/Fragment Analyzer/TapeStation) and Qubit quantification; aim for 0.25–0.5 ng/µL (max 2 ng/µL).

steps.title: Pilot: Design & validate pre‑amp primers
steps.instruction: Design, order, and bulk‑test pre‑amplification genotyping primers for gDNA and optionally cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Design ≥2 primer pairs per locus using Primer3/Primer‑Blast with: amplicon 200–900 bp, primer length 19–25 bp, Tm 57–63 °C, GC 20–80 %, 3.5 mM Mg²⁺, intron‑adjacent (gDNA) or exon‑adjacent (cDNA) where possible; re‑constitute at 100 µM in TE (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 0.1 mM EDTA).
Prepare 4 µM working dilutions in nuclease‑free water.

Prepare 2× mock RT buffer for 750 reactions (per reaction: 0.5 µL 40 % PEG 8000, 0.03 µL 10 % Triton X‑100, 0.1 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.3, 0.12 µL 1 M NaCl, 0.1 µL 100 mM MgCl₂, 0.04 µL 100 mM GTP, 0.32 µL 100 mM DTT, 0.79 µL nuclease‑free water). Warm Triton and water to 56 °C before mixing.

Set up bulk PCR (1 reaction): 5 µL 2× KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix, 2 µL 2× mock RT buffer, 1 µL gDNA (~5 ng/µL) or cDNA (~300 ng/µL), 1 µL forward 4 µM primer, 1 µL reverse 4 µM primer. Include NTC and positive control.
PCR program: 98 °C 3 min; 40 × (98 °C 20 s, 67 °C 30 s, 72 °C 6 min); 72 °C 5 min; hold 12 °C.
Run products on 2 % agarose gel; select primer pair with strongest, specific band.

steps.title: Pilot: Design & validate nested primers
steps.instruction: Design, order, and bulk‑test nested genotyping primers for each locus.

substeps.instruction: Design ≥2 nested primer pairs per locus (amplicon 150–500 bp, one primer within 140 bp of mutation, same length/Tm/GC criteria as pre‑amp primers). For gDNA, keep primers nested within pre‑amp primers; for cDNA, nest within cDNA pre‑amp primers.
Re‑constitute at 100 µM in TE; prepare 5 µM working dilutions (90 µL water + 5 µL each primer).
Set up bulk nested PCR (1 reaction): 3.125 µL KAPA 2G ReadyMix, 0.375 µL 5 µM primer pair, 1.5 µL template (gDNA ~5 ng/µL or cDNA ~300 ng/µL), 1.25 µL nuclease‑free water.
PCR program: 95 °C 3 min; 35 × (95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 20 s, 72 °C 1 min); 72 °C 5 min; hold 12 °C.
Run on 2 % agarose gel; choose best pair. If needed, combine one nested with one pre‑amp primer to rescue weak pairs.

steps.title: Pilot: Validate primers in single cells
steps.instruction: Test pre‑amp and nested primers in single‑cell RT‑PCR and assess cDNA and genotyping amplicon generation.

substeps.instruction: Sort single cells into plates prepared in Preparation 1 (generic lysis buffer). Keep plates on dry ice.

Perform protease inactivation and RT‑PCR pre‑amplification as in Part 3, but double all volumes (≈20 µL per well after PCR). Prepare separate RT mixes for each primer combination plus a positive control without genotyping primers; dispense each mix into a single column of the 96‑well plate.

After RT‑PCR, dilute each well 1:2 with nuclease‑free water, then purify 20 µL of the diluted material with AMPure XP beads as described in Preparation 1 step 5. Store purified cDNA at –20 °C (≤6 months).
QC cDNA by capillary electrophoresis; optimal traces indicate primers did not interfere.

Genotyping PCR1 test: for each nested primer pair, set up 1.5 µL of 5 µM primer mix + 1.5 µL KAPA 2G Robust HS ReadyMix + 1.5 µL nuclease‑free water per reaction (total 5 µL). Transfer 1.5 µL diluted cDNA‑amplicon mix from each well into the PCR1 reaction (minimum 6 wells per condition). Include bulk gDNA/cDNA positive control and NTC.
Run PCR1 with program: 95 °C 3 min; 20 × (95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 20 s, 72 °C 1 min); 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C.
Optionally set up multiplexed PCR1 reactions (≤4 loci per reaction).
Run PCR1 products on 2 % agarose gel; accept primers that give ≥5/6 strong, specific bands per locus. Redesign failing primers.

steps.title: Prepare barcoded primers for experiment
steps.instruction: Order and reconstitute all primers needed for the main TARGET‑seq+ run.

substeps.instruction: Order 384‑well barcoded oligo(dT)-ISPCR primers (Table S2); re‑constitute at 100 µM in TE; store at –80 °C.
Order HPLC‑purified target‑specific pre‑amp genotyping primers (validated in Preparations 2–4); re‑constitute at 100 µM in RNase‑free TE; store at –20 °C.

Order Access Array Barcode Library for Illumina Sequencers‑384 (four 96‑well plates, 2 µM per well). Aliquot 20 µL of each 2 µM primer pair into fresh 384‑well “stock” plates (quadrant layout); store at –20 °C.
Order custom sequencing primers (CS1, LCS1, CS2, CS2rc, P5‑seq, i5‑seq); re‑constitute at 100 µM in RNase‑free TE; make single‑use 100 µM aliquots; store at –20 °C (LNA‑modified primers at –80 °C).
Handle all primers in a pre‑PCR clean area with RNase‑free tips.

steps.title: Prepare barcoded lysis buffer (384‑well)
steps.instruction: Make 384‑well plates containing 1× lysis buffer with a unique barcoded oligo(dT)-ISPCR primer per well.

substeps.instruction: Prepare lysis buffer (per well: 1.943 µL nuclease‑free water, 0.593 µL 40 % PEG 8000, 0.035 µL 10 % Triton X‑100, 0.0475 µL RNase inhibitor (0.5 U/µL), 0.237 µL 10 mM dNTPs each, 0.075 µL protease (27 mAU/mL), 0.015 µL ERCC 1:4e5, total 2.805 µL). Keep on ice.
Dispense 25 µL of this lysis buffer into alternate columns of a fresh 384‑well plate (leaving empty columns).

Thaw 10 µM barcoded oligo(dT)-ISPCR primer plate, spin 500 × g 10 s, then transfer 1.8 µL of each primer into the corresponding well of the lysis buffer plate (final 0.67 µM primer). Mix gently; avoid cross‑contamination.
Seal with PCR film, spin 500 × g 10 s, then transfer 3 µL of the barcoded lysis buffer into alternate columns of a sterile 384‑well “sorting” plate (192 wells per plate).
Centrifuge plates 500 × g 10 s, snap‑freeze on dry ice, store at –80 °C (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Sample prep & single‑cell sorting
steps.instruction: Thaw, stain, and sort single cells from frozen bone marrow or peripheral blood into barcoded lysis plates.

substeps.instruction: Day before sort: prepare FACS buffer, thawing media, and antibody dilutions.

Thaw cryopreserved samples (max 2 at a time) in 37 °C water bath until 70–80 % liquid; add 1 mL warm FBS dropwise, transfer to 15 mL tube, add 1 mL warm thawing media dropwise, wash cryovial with 1 mL thawing media, then add 6 mL thawing media (total 10 mL) with gentle hand‑mixing after each 2 mL addition.
Centrifuge 350 × g 10 min at 21 °C; remove supernatant, blot tube dry.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL ice‑cold FACS buffer, pass through 35 µm strainer, wash to 5 mL total if starting >20 M cells.
Count cells, keep ~500 k cells for unstained, single‑stained, and FMO controls on ice.
Centrifuge remaining cells 350 × g 5 min, remove supernatant leaving ~50 µL.
Add Human Fc‑blocking solution 1:20, incubate 4 °C 5 min.
Stain with antibody mix (add 50 µL if cell number ≤25 % of total); keep on ice, protect from light.

Load 384‑well plate holder on sorter (e.g., Sony MA900). Calibrate: sort 30 droplets into corners of an empty plate, adjust until droplets land in well centers, then sort 20 droplets into same wells to verify bottom‑well deposition.
Clean sorter surroundings with RNase‑away.
Thaw barcoded lysis plates, spin 500 × g 20 s, keep at 4 °C.

Sort single cells into the barcoded lysis plates using single‑cell purity mode (droplet before and after target must be empty, target must be in central 75 % of droplet). Sort at ≤10 events/s, keep plate at 21 °C, limit sorting time to ≤20 min per plate. Fill 176 wells per plate with sample cells, then sort wild‑type control cells into remaining 14–15 wells; leave 1–2 wells empty as NTCs.
Use index‑sorting to record fluorescence per cell.
Seal plates with aluminum adhesive, spin 500 × g 20 s, snap‑freeze on dry ice. Store at –80 °C (≤3 months).

steps.title: Whole‑transcriptome library preparation
steps.instruction: Generate 3′‑biased whole‑transcriptome libraries from pooled pre‑amplified cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Normalize each purified cDNA pool to 800 pg/µL: calculate water volume to dilute 2 µL cDNA to 800 pg/µL, add water, then add 2 µL cDNA to reach 800 pg/µL.
Prepare tagmentation mix per reaction (10 µL TD buffer + 5 µL ATM = 15 µL).
Add 5 µL normalized cDNA to 15 µL tagmentation mix, mix, incubate 55 °C 10 min.
Add 5 µL Neutralize Tagment (NT) buffer (or 0.2 % SDS if NT unavailable), mix.
Add 5 µL 2 µM i7 index primer and 5 µL 2 µM custom i5 index primer (unique per cDNA pool).
Add 15 µL Nextera PCR Master Mix (NPM); PCR program: 95 °C 30 s; 13 × (95 °C 10 s, 55 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s); 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C.

AMPure XP bead cleanup (first round): equilibrate beads 30 min at 21 °C, add 35 µL beads (0.7 ×) to each reaction, incubate 5 min, magnet 2 min, wash twice with 100 µL 80 % ethanol, air‑dry 3–5 min, elute in 35 µL EB, incubate 5 min, magnet 2–3 min, transfer supernatant to 24.5 µL fresh AMPure beads, repeat bead binding, washing, and elution steps (final elution 20 µL EB).
QC library size (Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA Kit or TapeStation D5000): expected average 600–850 bp; repeat bead cleanup if primer dimers observed.
Quantify with Qubit dsDNA HS assay; calculate molarity using average fragment size.
Pool equimolar libraries, dilute pooled pool to 4 nM.

Sequence on Illumina (NextSeq/HiSeq/NovaSeq): load 300 nM custom Read 1 primer (P5‑SEQ) and, if using i5, Index Read 2 primer; run 151 cycles Read 1 (cell barcode), 8 cycles i7 (plate barcode), 151 cycles Read 2 (cDNA), 8 cycles i5 (optional plate barcode). Do not exceed 15 cycles for Read 1. Include 5–10 % PhiX.

steps.title: Single‑cell genotyping library preparation
steps.instruction: Enrich and barcode genotyping amplicons from each cell through two PCR steps and purify the final libraries.

substeps.instruction: Thaw genotyping stock plates (containing diluted cDNA‑amplicon mix from Part 4) by centrifuging 3000 × g 3 min at 21 °C.

Prepare genotyping PCR1 primer mixes (example: Mix 1 for 3 gDNA primer pairs, Mix 2 for 2 cDNA primer pairs). For each 384‑well plate, combine 0.019 µL of each 100 µM primer (≈0.58 µL per primer) and bring to 1.637 µL water (total 1.757 µL per reaction). Prepare enough for the plate plus 15 % dead volume.

Prepare Genotyping PCR1 master mix per plate: 3.25 µL KAPA 2G Robust HS ReadyMix + 1.757 µL primer mix = 5.021 µL per reaction (10 % dead volume). Dispense 5 µL master mix into each well of a fresh 384‑well PCR1 plate (MANTIS HV chip).
Transfer 1.5 µL from the genotyping stock plate into the PCR1 plate (VIAFLO, 3× mix).
Seal both plates, spin 500 × g 10 s, snap‑freeze stock plate, run PCR1: 95 °C 3 min; 20 × (95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 20 s, 72 °C 1 min); 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C.
Optional pause: store PCR1 plates at –20 °C (≤3 months).

Prepare genotyping PCR2 plates: thaw Access Array 2 µM stock plate, spin 3000 × g 3 min at 21 °C, aliquot 1.2 µL of each 2 µM barcoded PCR2 primer into fresh 384‑well plates (VIAFLO), seal, spin 500 × g 10 s, keep on ice.

Prepare PCR2 master mix (per reaction): 0.6 µL 10× FastStart Buffer, 1.08 µL MgCl₂, 0.3 µL DMSO, 0.12 µL nucleotide mix, 1.84 µL water, 0.06 µL FastStart enzyme, 24 µL total 4 µL per well (add 4 µL to each well of PCR2 plate). Seal, spin 500 × g 10 s.
Transfer 1 µL PCR1 product into each corresponding well of the PCR2 plate (VIAFLO, 3× mix).
Seal PCR2 plate, spin 500 × g 10 s, snap‑freeze PCR1 plate, run PCR2: 95 °C 10 min; 10 × (95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 1 min); 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C.
Optional pause: store PCR2 plates at –20 °C (≤3 months).

Pool genotyping libraries: for each PCR2 plate, centrifuge 3000 × g 2 min, then pool 1 µL from every well of a row into one column of a fresh 384‑well “PCR2 pooling plate” (Mosquito HTS). After all rows are pooled, each column contains material from one full PCR2 plate.
Transfer each column into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube (≈384 µL per tube).

AMPure XP bead cleanup of pooled PCR2 libraries: equilibrate beads 30 min at 21 °C, add 80 µL beads (0.8 ×) to each tube, mix, incubate 5 min, magnet 2 min, wash twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol, air‑dry 2–5 min, elute in 50 µL EB, incubate 3 min, magnet 2–3 min, transfer supernatant to new LoBind tubes.
Quantify each library with Qubit dsDNA HS; assess size distribution (Bioanalyzer/TapeStation D1000, expected 50–900 bp, add 115 bp adapters).
Pool libraries at equimolar ratios (consider average size, concentration, number of amplicons); dilute final pool to 4 nM.

Sequence on Illumina (MiSeq or NextSeq) using custom sequencing primers (CS1/LCS1 for Read 1, CS2 for Read 2, CS2rc for Index Read). Include 5–10 % PhiX. Recommended configuration: 151 cycles Read 1 + 10 cycles Index Read + 151 cycles Read 2.
